name: Draw.io (diagrams.net)
tagline: Free browser based diagram editor for flowcharts, network maps, org charts and architecture drawings.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. The web editor is free and open source; paid tiers exist mainly as Atlassian Marketplace apps for Confluence and Jira.

verdictSummary: A coding agent can give you a node and edge canvas with drag, connect, label, undo, save to a local JSON file and export to SVG or PNG in one sitting. What it cannot give you in one sitting is the part that makes Draw.io actually pleasant: orthogonal edge routing that does not cross through boxes, snapping and alignment guides, hundreds of stencil libraries for AWS, Azure, UML and network gear, and clean .drawio and VSDX interop. Also worth saying out loud: Draw.io is already free and open source, so the sane move is to clone the repo and self-host it rather than reimplement it. The DIY build only wins if you want a stripped down editor that speaks your own file format and nothing else.
coreLoopDIY: A local canvas app where you drop labeled shapes, connect them with arrows, rearrange, and export the result to SVG, PNG or a JSON file on disk.
requirements: No accounts, no server, everything in localStorage plus file download
whatYouLose: Orthogonal edge routing, waypoints and connection anchors that behave under drag
Alignment guides, snapping, grouping, layers and the dozens of keyboard shortcuts power users live on
Stencil libraries for AWS, Azure, GCP, UML, BPMN, network and floor plan shapes
Import and export of .drawio, VSDX, Lucidchart and Gliffy files, so nobody can hand you a diagram
Confluence, Jira, Google Drive and OneDrive embedding, plus real time co-editing
moatNotes: The hard part was never the canvas, it was fifteen years of edge routing edge cases and a stencil catalog nobody wants to redraw.
whyPeopleStillPay: Most people do not pay for Draw.io at all, which is the honest headline. The money is in the Confluence and Jira marketplace apps, where teams pay so diagrams live next to the docs, render in the page, version with the page and survive the person who drew them leaving. That is an integration purchase, not an editor purchase, and no local build touches it.
notes: Building a Draw.io replacement to avoid paying for Draw.io is a strange hobby, since the real thing is Apache licensed and self-hostable in a single container.
prompt:
Build a local, single user diagram editor that runs entirely in the browser with no backend.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- React Flow for the canvas, nodes and edges
- Zustand for state
- Tailwind for styling
- No server, no database, no accounts, no telemetry, no API keys, no .env needed

Features in scope:
- Left palette with 6 shape types: rectangle, rounded rectangle, ellipse, diamond, cylinder, note. Drag onto canvas to create.
- Click a node to select, double click to edit its label inline. Labels wrap and the node grows to fit.
- Drag from a node handle to another node to create a directed edge. Edges use the smoothstep type and render an arrowhead.
- Double click an edge to add a label.
- Right panel inspector for the selected node or edge: fill color, stroke color, stroke width, font size, and for edges a dashed toggle.
- Multi select with shift drag, move selection together, delete with Backspace or Delete.
- Undo and redo with Cmd/Ctrl+Z and Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+Z, at least 50 steps of history.
- Snap to a 10px grid, visible dotted grid background, zoom and pan, and a fit to view button.
- Autosave the whole document to localStorage on every change, restore on load.
- Toolbar actions: New, Save to .json file download, Open from .json file, Export SVG, Export PNG at 2x.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build:
- Multiplayer, comments, cloud sync, sharing links, or any login
- Importing .drawio, VSDX or Lucidchart files
- Stencil libraries beyond the 6 basic shapes
- Mobile layout, just make it usable at 1280px and up

Deliverables: working app via npm run dev, a README with keyboard shortcuts, and the document schema documented in one short section so the JSON files stay readable by hand.
